summary: Rabbi Besser explores the spiritual significance of the term hashkafa, explaining how performing acts of tzedakah can shift one's perspective and invite Hashem's favor. He further examines the Yud Gimel Midot and the custom of Tashlich, emphasizing that these practices are intended to inspire us to emulate Hashem's attributes of mercy and kindness in our daily lives.
questions: Why does the word hashkafa often imply scrutiny or negative judgment?
How does giving tzedakah change the way Hashem looks at us?
What is the purpose of reciting the Yud Gimel Midot?
Why do we perform the custom of Tashlich?
How can we practically emulate Hashem's actions in our own lives?
